1. **Streaming writer → the commit message of this change.** It changes nothing users see, nothing about privacy and nothing about cost, so it's a technical choice you can undo. Name it in the commit ("streaming writer instead of buffered; easy to swap") and don't write a separate decision document.
2. **Paid-plan gating → the standing questions issue.** It changes what users see and what they pay, so the owner decides. Ask it in plain language with a default that stands if nobody objects, for example "ships on all plans unless you say otherwise." Don't build it until the owner says yes.
3. **Ugly helper → no artifact.** It works and this change doesn't need it touched, so don't file an issue. Drop it. Refactoring it now would also go beyond the scope of this change.
4. **Penetration test → the milestone checklist for "first customer live."** It's a check that blocks a named milestone, not current work. It closes when the test has run or when the owner accepts the risk for that milestone.
5. **Empty-report crash → an issue.** It's a defect, so it gets an issue even though nobody has picked it up. Better still, since the export is your change, fix it now with a test for the empty report and reference the fix in the commit. Then there's nothing to file.

I didn't find a project profile in the repo, so these are generic artifact names. Swap in your tracker's names for the standing questions issue and the milestone checklist.
